title: Part Five: Sovereignty and Who Checks It

sections.brief: Why the Holy See (not the city) is a subject of international law: Lateran Art. 2 recognised a standing older than 1929; relations kept 1870-1929 (16 to 27 states); 184 states + EU + Order of Malta (note of 9 Jan 2026); gaps (PRC, Saudi Arabia, Vietnam; Taiwan; China bishops deal 2018/2024; Palestine 2015; UK 1982, US 1984, Israel 1994); UN observer 1964 and res. 58/314 (2004); See Change campaign (2000); immunity in O'Bryan (2008/2010), Doe (2009/2010/2012) and J.C. v. Belgium (ECtHR 2021). Figures: time

The 2014 CRC and CAT reviews of the Holy See: treaties ratified; Tomasi's three-level defence; CRC findings (transfers, code of silence, no mandatory reporting, worldwide obligation) and doctrinal recommendations; Holy See reply ('takes note', 'interfere with Catholic Church teaching'); CAT figures (3,420/848/2,572), effective-control view, reply ('many positive outcomes', abuse not torture); limits of the check; reporting since 2011 (Tapsell, Dec 2025). Figures: compare

Corrects 'IOR exempt from EU AML rules': 2000 and 2009 EU Monetary Agreements, Art. 8 and the yearly annex (Decision 2025/898, 2024 AML package, 2028 deadline); AIF 2010, prudential supervision 2013, ASIF 2020; Egmont suspension 2019-20; MONEYVAL 2012 (9/16), progress 2013-17, 2021 (5 substantial/6 moderate; prosecution and confiscation weak), 2024 follow-up; ASIF 2024 figures; what the checks reach. Figures: compare, time
